evidence.command_or_count: 12 runs / 21 request rows: corpus 12 items 22,162 chars (4 kinds x3), 21 JSONL rows, occamy C0=5359 tok vs L1=2625 tok (net saving 19.8%), qwen C0=5359 vs L1=3324 (18.1%), correctness 3/3 on every arm/model cell, L1 fetch counts [2,2,2] on both models with exactly the two required items (K-2, M-1) in 3/3 reps - corpus NOT swept

next_unit_hint: Repeat with a WARM prefix cache on both arms: occamy served C0 at a 99.1% cache hit in every rep (5312/5359), which inverts the 18-20% cold-cache saving into a loss. Also sweep corpus size (3k/10k/30k chars) and needed fraction (2 of 12 vs 6 of 30) to locate the crossover, and give both models the same fetch protocol.
assumptions: The named technique is 'lazy instruction loading'. The word 'pointer' is never used for it in any artefact under experiments/agentic-lazy/; it appears only in the unit card, to record why the pre-existing 'pointer' arm is not token compression and must not be reused as L1.

qwen3.5-9b (:8014) has no tool-call parser: tools+tool_choice returns 400 'auto tool choice requires --enable-auto-tool-choice and --tool-call-parser to be set'. The server must not be restarted, so qwen's L1 arm uses a text-emulated fetch protocol (FETCH <id> / ANSWER), recorded per row as protocol=text_emulated; occamy uses native function calling (protocol=native_function_calling). This makes the L1 runs 3 rounds on qwen vs 2 on occamy, which is why qwen's fetch overhead is higher. Cross-model comparison is indicative, not clean.

Completion budget fixed at 2048 tokens for every arm and model, because both models spend the budget on hidden reasoning before any visible content (occamy emitted 239 reasoning tokens for a 239-token answer). A smaller budget truncates runs for reasons unrelated to the arm.

Fetched-body tokens are estimated from characters using the characters-per-token ratio each model realises on the L1 index (occamy 2.11, qwen 3.32); no tokenizer was available. The estimate is applied symmetrically to both models. Likely understates the body cost, since technical text tokenizes denser than the prose index measure.

The 'realised saving' is a COLD-CACHE figure. occamy served C0 at a 99.1% cache hit on all three reps, so C0's marginal cost in a warm deployment is far lower than 5359. RESULTS.md states this as the headline caveat and does not quote 18-20% as the saving.
Temperature 0 with 3 reps: every cell returned identical prompt tokens and identical completions, so the reps establish stability rather than variance. n=3 cannot detect small effects.
Correctness saturated at 3/3 on every cell, so this task does not separate the arms on accuracy. Recorded as a limitation of the task, not as evidence the arms are equally robust.

Task, corpus and ground truth were fixed before the first live run and were not altered afterwards; no tuning was done to make L1 win. The only post-hoc change was to harness.check_answer, which had a scoring bug (it stripped underscores that are part of the field names it matches, marking every answer wrong); it was fixed and verified red-to-green (correct answer -> True, wrong numbers -> False, empty -> False) before any row was counted, and the two rows scored by the buggy version were quarantined as scratch_rows_badchecker.jsonl and are excluded from every table.
Rows from superseded probe runs of the emulated protocol (fetch=1, answer leaked as native tool syntax) were dropped from rows.jsonl and runs.json; the recorded rows are the final protocol only.
qwen's cached_tokens is unmeasured, not zero: :8014 never populates prompt_tokens_details.
